setup.effects: Build and migrate local state, save the first owner and private settings, and retain existing owner, secrets and data on repeat setup. No provider request.

dev.effects: Run Oncall on a loopback address, applying local migrations and printing a private RER_OPEN owner entry. First launch confirms the read-only owner at /setup; later launches open the app. --as signed-out selects the signed-out persona; --login retains automatic owner entry for compatibility. Ordinary /signin email sign-in sends only through a configured remote mail provider with real credentials; no sender is configured by default. --stop stops the owned server.

deploy.effects: Deploy incident coordination to your own Cloudflare account, claim the configured owner and retire its one-time setup token. Requires Cloudflare credentials and configured remote sign-in mail. Paging stays OFF; keep your existing pager active. --remove --yes deletes owned resources and reads back their absence. --site publishes the separate Run site. --dry-run builds and validates locally, then reads target secret bindings with Cloudflare credentials, without provider writes. --site --dry-run builds the separate Run site with no provider request.

export.effects: Write a private local archive of supported durable records and import journal; exclude sessions, credentials and private settings. Stop dev and preview first.

import.effects: Require an empty local destination and explicit --yes; atomically restore validated records and journal, pause pending timers, hold handoff approvals and disable Business import intake. Credentials and sessions never transfer; new owners must explicitly map an archived administrator identity.

preview.effects: Serve the built Oncall app on a loopback address with local state and owner sign-in. Ordinary /signin email sign-in sends only through a configured remote mail provider with real credentials; no sender is configured by default. --stop stops the owned server.

health.meaning: The coordination Worker can read its database; this is not a paging delivery guarantee.
